chunks: And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Isma'il ibn Sahl, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hadrami, from al-Kahili, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).

He was asked about a man whose mother married him off while he was absent. He said: 'The marriage is valid; if the groom wishes, he may accept it, and if he wishes, he may reject it. If the groom rejects the marriage arranged by his mother, the dowry remains obligatory upon his mother.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a mother marries off her adult son without his presence or explicit consent?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of 'tazwij al-umm' (mother arranging marriage) for an adult son, establishing that while the contract is initially valid, it remains contingent upon the son's subsequent ratification (qabul). The ruling highlights the mother's role as an agent who bears the financial risk (mahr) if her agency is revoked, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that the adult male retains ultimate autonomy over his marital status even when represented by a female guardian.
